_comment: Validate-mode golden: design §9's leakage checker, resolved half.
Hand-written (no Clang needed, so this runs on every lane) because the
one thing it needs from the front end is a list, not an analysis: which
namespace qualifiers survived the reference-resolved mapping. `foreign`
below is that list, exactly as `generate --emit-ir` emits it.
`detail` is named in each kind of rendered fragment, so the contexts
differ as well as the messages: a synopsis -- which the roster half must
never be run over, and which is where the corpus's own case lands -- an
itemdecl, and an extracted *Equivalent to:* body. The body names it twice
and `cache_` twice, for one finding each: dedup is per name per fragment,
and it is the same dedup for both halves of the rule.
The body is also where the two halves meet. `cache_` is invisible because
a roster says so; `detail` is invisible because the front end resolved it
outside the specification. Neither reason is reachable from the other, and
the fixits differ accordingly -- a namespace is not something an author can
mark `\expos` or demote to prose.
Two negative controls, both in the Remarks. `impl` is a foreign namespace
*and* a documented class, and a documented declaration outweighs a hidden
one whichever way the name is hidden -- so it stays silent. `move`
matches nothing at all, which is the case that keeps the check from
reporting every std name and every template parameter in sight.
